newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss leasing firm takes Boeing away from Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Swiss leasing firm takes Boeing away from Vietnam.

text.p: Swiss-based charter company TEA Basle AG has withdrawn two Boeing 737-200 aircraft from Vietnam because Pacific Airlines failed to honour a leasing agreement, the company said on Wednesday.
TEA withdrew the first aircraft in February and a second one on May 12, TEA Chairman Markus Seiler told Reuters.
"Problems with the organisation and capital structure prompted this step" in February, he said, and the second jet was withdrawn this month "after more payments were overdue".
He would not say how much was overdue on the contract, which called for TEA to provide pilots and mechanics as well as the two jets.

In Hanoi, Pacific Airlines officials who declined to be named said one aircraft was flown out of Ho Chi Minh City on Tuesday morning -- reducing the state-controlled airline's fleet to just two Boeings.
They gave no details of how the wet-lease agreement had been broken, though an informed source said the airline had failed to make a large scheduled payment.
Pacific Airlines was set up as a rival to the national flag-carrier Vietnam Airlines when Hanoi's drive to reform the economy along market lines was just gathering momentum.

It flies on three domestic routes and also on routes to Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau. One company official said the loss of the Boeing 737-200 would cut Pacific Airline's weekly schedule to 17 flights from 20. REUTER MAS JEC
